description: Installation of stand alone frame with defibrillator and bleed kit cabinets for community use.
decision_conditions: The proposed standalone frame with cabinets, by virtue of its size, siting and finish, would appear as a visually intrusive and incongruous addition contributing to increased visual clutter within the street scene, which would fail to integrate appropriately with the historic context of the area. The proposal would add unjustified visual clutter to the street, detracting from the visual amenity of the Conservation Area as well as the street scene more generally.

The proposal would result in harm to the significance of a heritage asset, for which the public benefits would be limited, given there are already two defibrillator kits in the immediate vicinity of the application site, which overlap with the proposed development in terms of their catchment and purpose. As such, the outlined harm to the Conservation Area is not sufficiently justified. The proposal fails to respect the local context and character and appearance of the Conservation Area, and as such would be in direct conflict

The proposed standalone frame with cabinets, by virtue of its size and proximity in relation to the kerb, would obstruct vehicular users of the adjacent parking bay from safely opening vehicle doors without impediment. The proposal would hinder the accessibility of an existing parking bay, the knock-on effects of which would result in the deterioration of safety and convenience for road users. The proposal is therefore considered to have an unacceptable impact on highway safety, and would accordingly conflict with Policy DMT 2 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part Two - Development Management Policies (2020), Policy T4 of the London Plan (2021), and Policy TR6 4 of the NPPF (2026).

waste_details.reason_for_no_provision: This is an application for installation of life saving equipment only
